rules.reason: All five inherited positive mechanisms are supported by the source-reviewed D analysis and current README/cache/getter/controller/Promise code. No persistence-boundary or unrelated cancellation scope is added.

R-task and I-entry-boundary prohibit live-signal invocation for the specific fresh, unentered online-mode offline departure. Body explicitly qualifies this situation and does not require zero entry. Coordination of settlement/restoration/resource termination is read as preserving the existing semantics when cancellation is used, not an unsupported demand to cancel/settle every paused or never-entered task.

R-background, F-boundary and F-creation distinguish active unconsumed background completion from fresh initial work; both actual AUTO cache regressions are counterexamples to a blanket unstarted/paused retirement predicate. The phrase according to existing rules retains later consumption/cancellation restrictions, rather than making all cached work immortal. Multiple patch changes do not isolate a root cause.

F-ownership explicitly shows the getter mutates shared query consumption but returns the current attempt controller. F-creation shows invocation resets the shared marker, while creating a new attempt does not. The rule forbids inferring record migration/reset merely from resource locality; it does not prohibit the existing invocation-time reset, mandate retaining unused fields, or prescribe a universal storage implementation.

README/R-background and F-events/F-boundary retain multiple observers, inert unknown unsubscribe, consumed-flight cancellation/revert, unconsumed active completion and late-generation isolation. These are requirements/source-preservation facts, not inference from pass/fail names.

R-task/I-entry-boundary support both permitted entry outcomes. R-entry/R-background and original-versus-AUTO raw checks support separate verification of cache resumption, delayed actual consumption, timing/state and reuse. It does not claim either AUTO patch is a complete fix or that isolated causation is proven.
